events.continuity_hook: Continues the New York family weekend after the Friday-to-Sunday dates are confirmed and rates are starting to move.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the flight-and-hotel package Maya should hold or book, with the tradeoff between airport convenience, room comfort, breakfast, and Sunday return timing made clear.
events.scenario_brief: Maya and her spouse have ruled out adding Thursday night, so the choice is now between the remaining Friday, December 11 to Sunday, December 13 packages for three travelers. The Friday midday ATL-to-LGA nonstop costs more than the Newark option but avoids arriving late with their child, while the late-afternoon Sunday return keeps a short final morning without pushing bedtime too far. The Midtown limited-service hotel includes breakfast and has strong guest ratings but small rooms; the Upper West Side boutique is calmer with better neighborhood restaurants but paid breakfast and a higher all-in cost. The remaining decision is whether schedule simplicity and included breakfast justify paying more than the Newark-and-boutique combination.

events.continuity_hook: Final logistics pass for the New York family weekend after the major bookings are in place.
events.interaction_goal: Build a concise family travel checklist covering seats, airport timing, hotel arrival, breakfast, weather, holiday crowds, and return-day transportation.
events.scenario_brief: A week before the New York weekend, Maya has booked the Friday midday ATL-to-LGA nonstop, the late-afternoon Sunday return, and the Midtown breakfast-included hotel. The hotel confirms breakfast hours and luggage storage, but the room is compact and bed setup still needs a final check. A cold, wet forecast and holiday street closures could affect airport transfers and walking plans, and she wants to make sure seats are together while keeping a window seat if possible. The unresolved items are whether to prebook an airport ride, how much margin to leave for the Sunday trip back to the airport, and whether any better seats have opened.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new work-travel episode once the December leisure trip wraps and January client dates appear.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Phoenix trip, identify realistic flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details Maya needs before sending a plan for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After the New York weekend, Maya is asked to start planning a solo Phoenix client workflow rehearsal for Monday, January 25 through Thursday, January 28. The client has not yet confirmed whether sessions will be at the central hospital campus or a Scottsdale outpatient site, and Monday may be remote unless a late-afternoon kickoff is added. ATL-to-PHX nonstops are available, though the cheaper one-stop choices create longer travel days. She wants an outbound that avoids an unnecessary early start, a Thursday return that leaves room after the closeout, and a well-reviewed hotel with easy breakfast and dinner options. The open questions are the first required in-person time, the exact site, and whether rideshares are enough or a rental car will be needed.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Phoenix planning after the client confirms the main site and meeting schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight, hotel, and local-transport combinations and choose the package Maya should send to her manager for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the central Phoenix hospital campus, a Monday 3:00 p.m. kickoff, Tuesday and Wednesday sessions from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and a Thursday closeout expected to end around noon. The most practical outbound is a late-morning Delta nonstop that lands with enough cushion for hotel luggage drop and the kickoff; the cheaper one-stop arrives too late to be comfortable. Thursday options include a midafternoon nonstop that feels tight and an early-evening nonstop that protects the closeout. Hotel choices include a central full-service property with strong ratings, on-site dining, and paid breakfast; a limited-service hotel with included breakfast but a longer rideshare each morning; and a downtown option with more restaurants but a less direct commute.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Phoenix work trip from approval into booking before the fare hold expires.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Phoenix flights, hotel booking notes, no-car plan, receipt details, and seat selections.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the late-morning outbound nonstop, the early-evening Thursday return, and the central full-service hotel as long as the rate remains cancellable. The client adds a Tuesday team dinner near the hospital campus, which makes the central hotel more useful despite paid breakfast. The fare hold expires that night, the hotel can add a quiet-room request away from elevators, and rideshares should cover the airport and campus transfers. Seat maps show a few window seats toward the back of both flights, while more forward seats are mostly aisles or middles.

events.continuity_hook: Adjusts the Phoenix logistics after a partial site change without reopening the whole trip.
events.interaction_goal: Update the Phoenix travel checklist and decide whether the new Wednesday site requires a transportation change or can be handled with the client shuttle and rideshares.
events.scenario_brief: About ten days before departure, the client updates the Phoenix agenda: most sessions remain at the central hospital campus, but Wednesday afternoon will move to a Scottsdale outpatient site for a live workflow walkthrough. A client shuttle may be available from the hospital, though the pickup time is not yet firm, so Maya needs to decide whether to keep the no-car plan or price a one-day rental as a backup. The booked flights and central hotel still fit, and the hotel confirms luggage storage, on-site dinner service, and paid breakfast only. The remaining items are Wednesday transportation, early breakfast alternatives, Atlanta airport timing, Thursday airport departure margin, and whether better window seats have opened.
